title: Not-for-Profit Accounting Final Review
description: Review contributions, donor restrictions, conditional gifts, donated services, endowments, and pledges.
html:
The NFP Big Picture

Not-for-profit accounting questions often revolve around one central issue:

WHO IMPOSED THE LIMITATION AND IS IT A RESTRICTION OR A CONDITION?

Correctly identifying those two concepts solves a large portion of NFP contribution questions.

Net Asset Classes

NFP financial statements generally present two classes of net assets.

NET ASSETS ↓ WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS + WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Who Creates a Donor Restriction?

A donor-imposed restriction can limit how or when contributed resources may be used.

Internal decisions by the board generally do not create donor-restricted net assets.

DONOR LIMITATION → MAY CREATE DONOR-RESTRICTED NET ASSETS BOARD DESIGNATION → GENERALLY REMAINS WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Restrictions vs Conditions

These terms are not interchangeable.

RESTRICTION → LIMITS HOW OR WHEN RESOURCES MAY BE USED CONDITION → MUST BE OVERCOME BEFORE ENTITLEMENT EXISTS

Conditional Contribution

A contribution is generally conditional when the agreement includes:

A BARRIER + RIGHT OF RETURN OR RIGHT OF RELEASE

Until the barrier is substantially overcome, the organization generally does not recognize contribution revenue.

Example — Conditional Grant

An organization receives $100,000 cash from a donor.

The organization must provide services to 500 participants, and the donor has the right to require repayment if the requirement is not met.

Only 300 participants have been served.

BARRIER NOT YET OVERCOME → NO CONTRIBUTION REVENUE YET

Because the cash has already been received, the organization generally records a liability.

Cash + $100,000
Refundable Advance / Liability + $100,000
Contribution Revenue $0

Once the Condition Is Met

When the barrier is overcome, the contribution becomes unconditional.

At that point, the organization evaluates whether a donor restriction still applies.

CONDITION SATISFIED → RECOGNIZE CONTRIBUTION THEN DETERMINE WHETHER DONOR RESTRICTION EXISTS

Unconditional Contributions

An unconditional contribution is generally recognized when the donor makes the promise or transfers the resources, subject to measurement requirements.

Restricted Contribution Example

A donor gives an organization $150,000 specifically for a scholarship program.

CONTRIBUTION REVENUE = $150,000 CLASSIFICATION = WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Release From Restriction

When the organization satisfies the donor's purpose or time restriction, the restriction is released.

This is a reclassification between net asset classes, not new contribution revenue.

WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS ↓ WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Example — Release

The organization spends $60,000 on the qualifying scholarship program.

RELEASE FROM RESTRICTION = $60,000

The organization does not recognize another $60,000 of contribution revenue simply because the restriction was satisfied.

Promises to Give

Unconditional promises to give are generally recognized when made.

UNCONDITIONAL PROMISE → RECOGNIZE CONDITIONAL PROMISE → WAIT UNTIL THE BARRIER IS SUBSTANTIALLY OVERCOME

Long-Term Pledges

An unconditional pledge expected to be collected over multiple years may require present-value measurement.

Face amount of pledge: $200,000

Present value: $176,000

INITIAL CONTRIBUTION RECEIVABLE = $176,000

Donated Services

Donated services are not automatically recognized simply because volunteers provided them.

Contributed services are generally recognized when they:

CREATE OR ENHANCE A NONFINANCIAL ASSET OR REQUIRE SPECIALIZED SKILLS + ARE PROVIDED BY PERSONS POSSESSING THOSE SKILLS + WOULD OTHERWISE NEED TO BE PURCHASED

Example — Donated Legal Services

An attorney provides legal services with a fair value of $25,000.

The organization would otherwise have hired an attorney to perform those services.

Contribution Revenue + $25,000
Legal Expense + $25,000
Net Assets No Net Change

Routine Volunteer Services

Routine volunteer services that do not meet the recognition criteria generally are not recognized as contribution revenue or expense.

VOLUNTEER TIME ≠ AUTOMATIC RECOGNITION

Donated Noncash Assets

Contributed nonfinancial assets such as equipment, supplies, or property are generally recognized at fair value, subject to applicable accounting guidance.

Donated equipment fair value: $70,000

EQUIPMENT = $70,000 CONTRIBUTION REVENUE = $70,000

Endowments

Endowment accounting depends heavily on whether the restriction was imposed by the donor or internally by the organization.

DONOR-RESTRICTED ENDOWMENT → NET ASSETS WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS BOARD-DESIGNATED ENDOWMENT → GENERALLY NET ASSETS WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Investment Return

Investment income associated with an endowment must be classified according to applicable donor restrictions and governing requirements.

Do not automatically assume that all investment income is unrestricted.

Example — Restricted Endowment Return

A donor-restricted endowment earns:

Interest and dividends: $20,000

Appreciation: $15,000

Donor requires returns to support scholarships.

TOTAL INVESTMENT RETURN = $20,000 + $15,000 = $35,000

The classification of that return reflects the donor restriction until the applicable restriction is satisfied.

NFP Financial Statements

Core NFP financial statements commonly include:

STATEMENT OF FINANCIAL POSITION STATEMENT OF ACTIVITIES STATEMENT OF CASH FLOWS

Statement of Activities

The statement of activities reports changes in the organization's net assets.

REVENUES + GAINS − EXPENSES − LOSSES = CHANGE IN NET ASSETS

Functional Expense Classification

Expenses may be classified by function.

PROGRAM SERVICES + SUPPORTING SERVICES

Supporting services can include management and general activities and fundraising.

Natural Expense Classification

Natural classification describes what type of cost was incurred.

EXAMPLES: SALARIES RENT DEPRECIATION SUPPLIES INTEREST

Functional vs Natural

FUNCTION → WHY WAS THE COST INCURRED? NATURE → WHAT TYPE OF COST WAS IT?

Integrated NFP Example

Beginning net assets:

Without donor restrictions: $500,000

With donor restrictions: $180,000

During the year:

Unrestricted contribution: $100,000

Restricted contribution: $90,000

Qualifying restricted spending: $50,000

Other expenses: $70,000

Ending Restricted Net Assets

$180,000 + $90,000 − $50,000 = $220,000

Ending Unrestricted Net Assets

$500,000 + $100,000 + $50,000 RELEASE − $70,000 EXPENSES = $580,000

NFP Decision Strategy

ASK: 1. IS THIS A CONTRIBUTION OR AN EXCHANGE TRANSACTION? 2. IS THE CONTRIBUTION CONDITIONAL? 3. IF UNCONDITIONAL, IS THERE A DONOR RESTRICTION? 4. HAS THE RESTRICTION BEEN SATISFIED? 5. DOES THE TRANSACTION AFFECT REVENUE, EXPENSE, OR ONLY NET-ASSET CLASSIFICATION?

Common FAR Traps

CONDITION ≠ RESTRICTION BOARD DESIGNATION ≠ DONOR RESTRICTION RELEASE FROM RESTRICTION ≠ NEW REVENUE DONATED SERVICES ≠ AUTOMATIC RECOGNITION

Key Takeaways

  • NFPs report net assets with donor restrictions and without donor restrictions.
  • Board designations generally do not create donor-restricted net assets.
  • A conditional contribution generally requires both a barrier and a right of return or release.
  • Once a contribution becomes unconditional, donor restrictions are evaluated separately.
  • Satisfaction of a donor restriction generally results in a reclassification, not additional contribution revenue.
  • Unconditional promises to give are generally recognized when made.
  • Qualifying donated professional services are recognized at fair value.
  • Donor-restricted endowments remain within net assets with donor restrictions until applicable restrictions are met.
  • Functional classification describes why a cost was incurred; natural classification describes the type of cost.

quiz.prompt: A donor gives an NFP $120,000 restricted for a specific education program. During the year, the NFP spends $45,000 on qualifying program costs. Ignoring all other activity, how much of the original contribution remains in net assets with donor restrictions?
quiz.explanation: The organization initially recognizes the $120,000 contribution within net assets with donor restrictions. When $45,000 is spent for the donor-specified purpose, that amount is released from restriction. The remaining donor-restricted amount is $120,000 − $45,000 = $75,000.
